title: Scalar extension and semilocal principal parts on a smooth curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $C/k$ a smooth projective geometrically connected curve [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Put $C_K=C\times_k K$ [def-pc-base-change], $F=k(C)$ and $L=K(C_K)$ [def-sc-function-field]. Let $x$ be a closed point of $C$, $O=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, and $S$ the set of points of $C_K$ over $x$. Then $C$ and $C_K$ are integral, $O$ and $O_y=\mathcal O_{C_K,y}$ for $y\in S$ are discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and their residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] are finite over $k$ and $K$, respectively. The set $S$ is finite and nonempty and is canonically the underlying point set of $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x)\otimes_k K)$; all its points are closed in $C_K$. The canonical map $V=F\otimes_k K\to L$ is injective. Regard $A=O\otimes_k K\subset V\subset L$ and $B=\bigcap_{y\in S}O_y\subset L$. For every uniformizer $t$ of $O$ and every $n\ge1$, the canonical maps give isomorphisms
$$(O/t^nO)\otimes_k K\ \simeq\ A/t^nA\ \simeq\ B/t^nB\ \simeq\ \prod_{y\in S}O_y/t^nO_y,$$
and these are finite-dimensional $K$-algebras. Moreover $V=A[t^{-1}]$, $L=B[t^{-1}]$, $V\cap B=A$, and the canonical maps of $K$-vector spaces are isomorphisms
$$V/A\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ L/B\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \bigoplus_{y\in S}L/O_y.$$
The first map is induced by inclusion and the second by the diagonal map. No reduction of the finite algebras in these formulas is taken.

source.place: Algebra Tags 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder), 00JB (algebra-lemma-artinian-finite-length), 034X (algebra-lemma-characterize-Dedekind): semilocal principal-parts consequence after flat field extension; agent synthesis explained in report.md.

proof.text: $C$ is integral and of dimension one by the definition of a smooth projective curve. Projectivity gives properness, and properness gives finite type. The field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $C$ is Noetherian. Smoothness and properness persist over $K$; the same argument gives finite type and Noetherianity of $C_K$. Both schemes are regular by smoothness over a field. The relative-dimension-one base-change lemma, first with $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and then with $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$, gives $\dim_z C=1$ and $\dim_z C_K=1$ at every point, in the topological local-dimension sense. Geometric connectedness gives connectedness of $C_K$; its nonemptiness is established in step 3 before invoking the integral criterion.

Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$, and let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal. The affine stalk identification gives $O=R_{\mathfrak m}$ and $\kappa(x)=R/\mathfrak m$. The closed-point field lemma gives $d=[\kappa(x):k]<\infty$. The closed-point dimension lemma and step 1 give $\dim O=1$; regularity then gives that $O$ is a DVR. These arguments use a finite type affine chart, not an arbitrary local ring of a curve.

The affine fibre product identifies the fibre over $x$ with $\operatorname{Spec}T_1$, where $T_1=(R/\mathfrak m)\otimes_kK=\kappa(x)\otimes_kK$: the quotient maps kill precisely the ideal generated by $\mathfrak m$, by the universal property of tensor products and quotients. A $k$-basis of $\kappa(x)$ becomes a $K$-basis of $T_1$, so $T_1$ has positive dimension $d$. Apply the finite-algebra spectrum lemma with base $K$, a local ring whose only prime is $(0)$. It gives finitely many primes, all maximal, with intersection the nilradical. Thus the product-of-localizations lemma applies. Its product cannot be empty, since the empty product is the zero ring and $T_1\ne0$. Therefore $S$ is finite and nonempty. Each point is closed in the fibre, which is the inverse image of the closed subset $\{x\}$, hence closed in $C_K$. Its residue field is finite over $K$ by the closed-point field lemma. In particular $C_K$ is nonempty. Regularity and connectedness from step 1 now imply its integrality.

source.place: Tag 00JA; proof of Tag 06RS (lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian), using Tags 05DR and 00GT; Schemes Tag 01I4; Properties Tags 0569 and 033N

proof.text: Put $R_K=R\otimes_kK$. The affine chart $U_K$ is nonempty, and its ring $R_K$ is a domain because $C_K$ is integral. The function-field lemma identifies $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}R_K$. The localization-tensor comparison identifies $A$ with $(R\setminus\mathfrak m)^{-1}R_K$ and $V$ with $(R\setminus\{0\})^{-1}R_K$. No nonzero element of $R$ becomes zero in $R_K$: extend the singleton consisting of that element to a $k$-basis and tensor that basis with $K$. Hence both localizations inject into $L$, giving the canonical inclusions $A\subset V\subset L$. A point $y\in S$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q_y$ of $R_K$ over $\mathfrak m$. Set $\mathfrak p_y=\mathfrak q_y A$. The affine stalk formula and iterated fractions give $O_y=(R_K)_{\mathfrak q_y}=A_{\mathfrak p_y}$, compatibly inside $L$. Since $y$ is closed, the closed-point dimension lemma and step 1 give $\dim O_y=1$, and its regularity makes it a DVR. Localizing a domain does not change its fraction field, so the fraction fields of $O$ and $O_y$ are $F$ and $L$.

source.place: Tags 01I4 and 01HV; Algebra Tags 00E3 and 00OU; Morphisms Tag 01RV

proof.text: Fix a uniformizer $t$ of $O$. For every $n\ge1$, the map $(O/t^nO)\otimes_kK\to A/t^nA$ sends $\bar a\otimes c$ to the class of $a\otimes c$. It is an isomorphism: choose a $k$-vector-space complement to $t^nO$ in $O$; tensoring this direct-sum decomposition identifies the kernel of $O\otimes_kK\to(O/t^nO)\otimes_kK$ with $(t^nO)\otimes_kK$, whose image is exactly $t^nA$. This also verifies the asserted canonical map, independently of the chosen complement. The filtration by $t^iO/t^nO$, $0\le i\le n$, has successive quotients $\kappa(x)$: multiplication by $t^i$ induces $O/tO\simeq t^iO/t^{i+1}O$, since $O$ is a domain. Thus $O/t^nO$ has $k$-dimension $nd$ and $Q_n=A/t^nA$ has $K$-dimension $nd$. In particular $Q_n\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), parameter filtration; tensor quotient calculation by direct-sum complements

proof.text: By step 5, $Q_n=A/t^nA$ is a finite $K$-algebra. Apply the finite-algebra spectrum lemma with base $K$ to obtain a finite maximal spectrum and a locally nilpotent Jacobson radical. The product-of-localizations lemma therefore gives its canonical product decomposition. Every prime of $Q_n$ contains the image of $t$, since $t^n=0$ there, so its primes correspond exactly to those of $A/tA=T_1$, hence to $S$. Concretely primes of a quotient are inverse images of primes containing its kernel: both assignments preserve products and properness and are inverse. Each factor $(Q_n)_{\mathfrak p_y/(t^n)}$ is canonically $A_{\mathfrak p_y}/t^nA_{\mathfrak p_y}=O_y/t^nO_y$. To check this last equality, send $\bar a/\bar s$ to the class of $a/s$, and send the class of $a/s$ back to $\bar a/\bar s$, for $s\notin\mathfrak p_y$. Fraction equality and the relation $t^n=0$ show these maps are well-defined and inverse. Consequently the product decomposition is precisely the canonical isomorphism $Q_n\simeq\prod_{y\in S}O_y/t^nO_y$.

source.place: Tag 00JA, proof of Tag 06RS (lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian), and Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient)

proof.text: By its definition $A\subset B=\bigcap_y O_y$. The diagonal $B\to\prod_yO_y/t^nO_y$ has kernel $\bigcap_y t^nO_y=t^nB$: dividing an element of the intersection by the common nonzero element $t^n$ puts it in every $O_y$. It is surjective, since its restriction to $A$ is surjective by step 6. Thus $B/t^nB$ maps isomorphically to that product. The composite from $A/t^nA$ is exactly step 6, so $A/t^nA\to B/t^nB$ is an isomorphism as well. Together with step 5 this proves every quotient isomorphism in the statement and their finite-dimensionality. All maps preserve multiplication and the structural image of $K$.

source.place: Tags 00JA and 00CT: application to the intersection, with kernel and surjectivity written out

proof.text: The DVR valuation description gives $F=O[t^{-1}]$: a nonzero fraction is a unit times an integral power of $t$. Tensoring the displayed fractions, or using the localization-tensor comparison, gives $V=A[t^{-1}]$. For every $y\in S$, $t$ is nonzero and lies in the maximal ideal of $O_y$ (its image vanishes in the fibre), so $v_y(t)>0$. For any $f\in L^*$ choose an integer $n\ge0$ with $n v_y(t)+v_y(f)\ge0$ for every $y$; this is possible since $S$ is finite. Then $t^nf\in B$, proving $L=B[t^{-1}]$. The same assertion for $f=0$ is immediate.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), integer valuations in the fraction field

proof.text: If $v\in V\cap B$, write $v=a/t^n$ with $a\in A$, $n\ge1$ (increase the denominator exponent if necessary). Then $a\in A\cap t^nB$. The injectivity of $A/t^nA\to B/t^nB$ in step 7 says $a\in t^nA$, so $v\in A$. Hence $V\cap B=A$, and inclusion induces an injection $V/A\to L/B$. For surjectivity write $f=b/t^n$ with $b\in B$, $n\ge1$, using step 8. Choose $a\in A$ congruent to $b$ modulo $t^nB$ by step 7. Then $f-a/t^n\in B$. The representative $a/t^n$ belongs to $V$, proving surjectivity.

source.place: Consequences of the quotient isomorphisms; common-denominator calculation

proof.text: The kernel of the diagonal map $L\to\bigoplus_{y\in S}L/O_y$ is $B$ by definition; the direct sum is the finite product because $S$ is finite. For any tuple of classes choose representatives $f_y\in L$. Choose a single $n\ge1$ with $t^nf_y\in O_y$ for all $y$, using the positive valuations in step 8. Step 6 supplies $a\in A$ whose class in $O_y/t^nO_y$ is $t^nf_y$ for every $y$. Consequently $a/t^n-f_y\in O_y$ for every $y$, so $a/t^n\in L$ maps to the given tuple. This proves the second canonical isomorphism. Both quotient maps are $K$-linear. Every quotient above is the actual ideal quotient; no nilpotent is discarded at any step.

A and V are identified by the localization-tensor lemma, and O_y=A_{p_y}. Steps 5-10 are correct and fully written: the tensor quotient has dimension nd.
